Mr. B. Hossain, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record ------ for the Respondent.
parties:
Hussain Md. Ershad ------ Appellants
Vs.
The State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
A T M Afzal, CJ: This appeal by leave is from judgment and order dated 10.12.96 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No. 5186 of 1996 refusing to enlarge the accused-appellant, Hussain Mohammad Ershad, a former President of Bangladesh, on bail in Special Case No. 154 of 1994 arising out of Cantonment P.S. Case No. 8(5)92 now pending in the Sixth Court of Additional Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Dhaka. 

 2. Besides the appellant, two former Chiefs of the Air Staff, namely, Sultan Mahmud and Momtazuddin Ahmed and two other persons, one being M. Shahajad Ali (who was subsequently discharged on the prayer of the Public Prosecutor) have been made accused in the charge sheet on the allegation, inter alia, that they in collusion with each other and misusing their official power purchased Radar for the Bangladesh Air Force from an U.S. Company rather than from a French Company ignoring the recommendation of the Radar Evaluation Team of 1981 and thereby caused loss to the Government of Bangladesh to the tune of Tk. 64, 04,42,918.10 and misappropriated the same for the purpose of making unlawful gain for themselves or for others and thus committed offences under section 409/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, Act No. 2 of 1947. The case was initiated by an officer of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption by lodging an FIR with the Cantonment P.S. on 4.5.92. 

 3. The gist of the allegation is that the two Air Chiefs were responsible for making the alleged recommendation for purchase following an initiative by a Former Air Chief in 1980 to purchase Radar from a French Company. On 23.9.86 the Defence Secretary submitted a case summary for necessary orders regarding the purchase of Radar before the appellant wherein he mentioned in details about the fact of proposed purchase of Radar in 1980 and refusal of the Ministry of Finance to provide fund to purchase the same at that time. He also mentioned that the Radar of the French Company (Thomson C.S.F.) is superior in quality than that of Westing House (U.S. Company), and Thomson C.S.F. proposed to supply the same at half price than Westing House. The said Company would also provide free training, spare parts and easier terms for payment of price. But the appellant in spite of knowing the entire facts from the case summary approved the proposal of purchasing 3 Radars from the Westing House Company through their agent M/s. Lot West Company as power revised proposal at a price of Tk. 64,04,42,918.10. 

 4. Following submission of charge-sheet by the Police, the learned Special Judge framed charge against the appellant and other accused under the aforesaid sections by order dated 12.8.95 whereupon co-accused Sultan Mahmud, A.K.M. Musa and Momtazuddin Ahmed filed Criminal Misc. Case Nos. 946196, 1204/96 and 2260/96 respectively before the High Court Division in which Rules were issued, records called for and further proceeding of the case was stayed. These cases are still pending. Co-accused Sultan Mahmud and Momtazuddin Ahmed were granted bail by the trial Court and AKM Musa was granted bail by the High Court Division. 

 6. It was, among other, argued in the High Court Division that the two co-accused, Chiefs of the Air Staff, having already been granted bail and that in the meantime one of them having been offered a diplomatic assignment as Ambassador (perhaps to show the changed attitude of the Government) there was no reason to refuse bail to the appellant. The appellant being on the same footing, he could not be discriminated against by refusing bail to him. The learned Judges agreed that as co-accused facing trial in the same case they stood on the same footing but also held that the appellant as a President had a greater responsibility and exalted position than that of the two former Air Chiefs. The learned Judges observed that the apprehension of the learned Special Judge as to the possibility of tampering with evidence by the appellant could not be ruled out lightly. It was also observed that the disposal of the main case was being blocked in a tactful and subtle manner by misusing the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Finally, the learned Judges said: "From the news media we learn that the (appellant) petitioner is leading very active life in the Parliament and in the sub-Jail specially arranged for him with special facilities." 

 8. Khondker Mahbub Hossain, learned Advocate for the appellant, submits that the High Court Division failed to exercise its judicial discretion properly in refusing bail to the appellant by taking into consideration unfounded, irrelevant and improper facts and circumstances and further in not considering the relevant ones. The High Court Division failed to apply the normal and usual tests which are germane for consideration in a prayer for bail. The refusal of bail to the appellant was apparently discriminatory in that the two other co-accused’s, namely, the Air Chiefs who were granted bail, were found to be on the same footing as that of the appellant. He submits that it was wishfully observed that the possibility of tampering with evidence could not be ruled out because the investigation was already complete and the evidence which is mostly documentary was in the custody of the Government and further there was no allegation on the part of the prosecution at any stage that the appellant was likely to tamper with the evidence if released on bail. The learned Advocate submits that the appellant is already on bail in all other cases except the present one and the refusal by the High Court Division to grant bail on the imaginary possibility of tampering with evidence was thoroughly injudicious. Mr. Hussain finally submits that having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case the refusal of bail to the appellant in the present case only has resulted in a miscarriage of justice. 

 10. Although charge was framed on 12.8.95 there has been no progress in the trial because of a stay order granted by the High Court Division in the Misc. Cases started by the co-accused which are still pending. This fact alone i.e., indefiniteness of trial is sufficient to allow the appellant to continue on the bail granted to him. However, it is necessary to make some comment on the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. Although the High Court Division itself found that the co-accused Air Chiefs and the appellant were on the same footing as accused, the appellant was denied bail because his responsibility in the matter as President was found to be higher. This was hardly a good judgment because it should have been realized that the President was not making a household purchase for himself but approving the purchase of Radar for the Air force as recommended by the Air Chiefs. The President's decision may have been wrong or motivated which is to be decided at the trial but for the purpose of bail there was no reason to discriminate between them. 

 12. The High Court Division was not fair in making scornful comment on the appellant on the basis of media report because whatever privileges he might have been given while in custody, it could not be equated with freedom. It has been argued that the appellant was not only a former President of the country but was elected Member of Parliament from five constituencies remaining in custody. Several cases of similar nature were brought against the appellant after his downfall but he was granted bail in all cases gradually, some by the High Court Division itself, except the present one and thus the impugned order was not at all justified, submitted his learned Advocate. 

 13. The learned Deputy Attorney General could not make much out of the impugned judgment except submitting that as the principal offender, the appellant's case for bail was rightly treated differently from others. 

 15. The appeal is accordingly allowed. The appellant shall continue to remain on the same bail pending disposal of the Special Case No. 155 of 1994.
